claim: AI now writes most of the new code, so an engineer is no longer paid for the code: you are paid for what the code does to the business, so be the engineer who owns a number.
why_this_claim: It is the thesis of the video in its own words (CH2 'Code got cheap, but outcomes didn't' plus the CH6 landing line) and it needs nothing else to stand: one sourced fact (the 75% at Google), the turn, the question the fact raises, the answer, the instruction. The pod, the funnel map and the four engineer versions all need their diagrams and minutes of setup; the market data is a second idea. This one argument closes inside 27 s and leaves the four versions as the reason to click through.

assembled_read: At Google, 75% of all new code is generated by AI. Engineers approve it. You just cannot keep your head down and write code anymore. So picture how much demand is left for an engineer who only wants to sit there and code. Code got cheap, but outcomes didn't. A company doesn't pay you for the code. It pays you for what the code does to the business. Don't be the engineer who only codes. Be the engineer who owns a number.

rejected.reason: 'That's Google's own CEO in April, 2026.' The attribution. 3.9 s that push the spans past 28 s; the Google page in span 1 already shows whose claim it is.

The Anthropic 'over 90%' line plus 'their own filing with the SEC'. A second number for the same point, 11.2 s, and it cannot be shortened (0.04 s gap before 'That's in their own filing'). The transcript also hears Claude as 'Clawed'.

'So the question isn't whether an AI writes the code. The question is what the software engineer's actually getting paid for.' (D1 question card). It asks what span 3 answers; question plus answer plus kicker runs over the budget, and the answer is the stronger half. Its in gap is 0.13 s inside the F2 cut-out burn.
C3 animated chart, Google 25% to 50% to 75%. 14 s, the chart is drawing for most of it, and the hook already says the 75%.

'Less typing, more directing, and more reviewing.' (D2 card). Clean gaps and only 2.7 s, but the card on screen is the Anthropic S-1 quote straight after a Google hook, and it would replace F2, the locked turn.

'Now one single engineer can fill almost all of those seats ... One engineer runs the whole pod.' (C2 pod diagram). A different claim, 'those seats' and 'the pod' have no referent cold, and the span would open on the C2 camera pan (153.40-154.25).
'I run a whole company this way ...' (D18 card over the blacked-out face). 'This way' has no referent cold; 12.6 s.

'Four engineers, not one of them is defined by a programming language or framework. Each one is defined by the outcome that they own.' on the finished C1 map. The best diagram in the video and clean troughs (0.31 s and 0.37 s), but 'Four engineers' has no referent cold and it costs 6.4 s: it only fits if F2 goes and span 3 loses its question. Kept as the swap in risks.
'Software jobs aren't disappearing.' (D13 head). Cuts clean and would fit, but it is the market idea, a second claim, and it softens the turn.
'The demand didn't disappear, it just moved.' (C4 payoff). No gap at all before 'The' (the word '10%.' runs into it) and the arrow sweep is mid-animation at 407.10-407.60.

F8 'If you're already in the market and you refuse to believe this change is real, then you're the one who gets left behind.' A strong warning, but 5 s over the budget with span 3 whole, troughs of only 0.22 s and 0.13 s, and a fifth face. The F9 kicker does the same job as an instruction.
'So here's what to do ... measure what it did to that number.' (D16, three steps). It defines 'a number', but it is 17.5 s and no part of it stands alone.
Subscribe ask and the end-screen pointer over D17. The short has its own CTA.
